question.text: For an AIF constituted as a trust, which combination of trust attributes is considered MOST APPROPRIATE from a tax-clarity perspective?

answer.text: Public charitable trust settled on family members
Revocable, indeterminate trust with the settlor as sole beneficiary

explanation.text: The Logic: AIF trusts are structured as 'irrevocably settled, determinate trusts'. 'Irrevocable' means the settlor cannot reclaim the corpus. 'Determinate' means the beneficial interest of each investor is clearly ascertainable — which is why the corpus is divided into units and investors are allotted specific numbers of units representing their determinate share. The Trap: 'Determinate' vs 'discretionary' is the key axis: a discretionary trust gives the trustee flexibility to decide distributions, which creates tax uncertainty and would jeopardise tax-clarity for an AIF. Revocable trusts would allow settlor to pull the corpus back — unacceptable to investors. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A, XIX-B, XIX-C and XIX-D all test this same attribute set. XXIV (AML) also touches on beneficial ownership which relates to the determinacy concept. Manager's Pro-Tip: As a Cat III manager, insist the trust deed is drafted so that each investor's unit-holding is the sole measure of their beneficial interest — this keeps the determinacy intact even when you open new series for HWM or create a side-pocket.
